s1.syndrome_frame: chronic ulcerative skin lesion with hyperkeratotic edges and unstructured whitish areas
salient_findings: painful, fissured ulcer at the base of the fourth interdigital space of the right foot
verrucous, infected ulceration with infiltrated, hyperkeratotic edges
unstructured whitish areas and hyperkeratosis on dermoscopy
key_facts: 60-year-old patient with no significant medical history
3-year history of macerated skin between toes
18-month history of progressively enlarging ulcer
received multiple antifungal regimens without improvement
ulcer measures 3 cm in diameter and extends onto the dorsum of the foot
hyperkeratotic edges and whitish, fissured base
dermoscopy reveals unstructured whitish areas and hyperkeratosis
no palpable popliteal and inguinal lymph nodes

shortlist.label: Squamous cell carcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: persistent and enlarging ulcer with hyperkeratotic edges

shortlist.label: Verrucous carcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: verrucous appearance and lack of response to antifungal treatment

shortlist.label: Chronic pyoderma gangrenosum
shortlist.why_kept: ulcerative skin lesion with progressive enlargement

shortlist.label: Keratoacanthoma
shortlist.why_kept: rapidly growing skin lesion with hyperkeratotic edges

shortlist.label: Basal cell carcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: persistent skin lesion with unstructured whitish areas

shortlist.label: Cutaneous T-cell lymphoma
shortlist.why_kept: persistent and enlarging skin lesion with atypical features

shortlist.label: Mycetoma
shortlist.why_kept: chronic and progressive skin lesion with possible fungal infection

shortlist.label: Sporotrichosis
shortlist.why_kept: skin lesion with lymphatic spread and lack of response to antifungal treatment

raw.rationale: The patient's presentation of a verrucous, infected ulceration with infiltrated, hyperkeratotic edges and a whitish, fissured base, along with dermoscopy revealing unstructured whitish areas and hyperkeratosis, is consistent with verrucous carcinoma, a type of low-grade malignancy that can resemble a wart and is often resistant to antifungal treatments.

rejected.label: Squamous cell carcinoma
rejected.why: While possible, the description of the ulcer as verrucous and the dermoscopy findings are more suggestive of verrucous carcinoma.

rejected.label: Chronic pyoderma gangrenosum
rejected.why: Typically presents with painful ulcers but lacks the verrucous appearance and dermoscopy findings seen in this case.

rejected.label: Keratoacanthoma
rejected.why: Usually has a more rapid growth phase and a central crater-like appearance, not described in this case.

rejected.label: Basal cell carcinoma
rejected.why: Less likely given the location and appearance of the ulcer, as well as the lack of typical basal cell carcinoma features like pearly borders or telangiectasias.

rejected.label: Cutaneous T-cell lymphoma
rejected.why: Would typically present with more systemic symptoms and different skin manifestations, such as patches, plaques, or tumors, not a single ulcerative lesion.

rejected.label: Mycetoma
rejected.why: Involves deeper tissue and typically presents with sinus tracts and discharge, not described in this case.

rejected.label: Sporotrichosis
rejected.why: Usually presents with lymphocutaneous spread and multiple lesions along the path of lymphatic drainage, not a single ulcer as seen here.
